grh_b4beca804b5a93c7d83e.title: Tanzy Story
paragraphs: Mrs. Tansy has spent years doing everything for a household of grown children and in-laws who love her but take her labor completely for granted. They plan a birthday supper in her honor without noticing that she will still be expected to cook it, clean up and continue waiting on everyone. When Christian sees how thoughtlessly they depend on her, he makes the family believe her heart requires complete rest and orders her to bed. Faced for the first time with cooking, housekeeping and supporting themselves without Mrs. Tansy, the family members are forced into responsibility: the unemployed son-in-law must work, the daughter has to use her business training, and the children learn how much their mother has quietly been doing. Mrs. Tansy improves while the household learns to function around her instead of through her. Christian later admits that she had not actually been ill; putting her to bed was his way of teaching the family what life would be like without her and of making them appreciate her before it was too late.

The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Rosemary De Camp, and [[person|gale-gordon|Gale Gordon]]. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_b49e2885bdfcb160326f.title: Jezebel
paragraphs: Proud New Orleans belle Julie Marsden repeatedly tests and humiliates her fiancé Pres Dillard until her defiance destroys their engagement. When Pres later returns married to Amy, Julie tries to reclaim him and provokes jealous rivalries that end in a fatal duel. A yellow-fever epidemic then strikes New Orleans and Pres falls gravely ill. Realizing the damage her selfishness has caused, Julie asks Amy to let her accompany Pres to the deadly quarantine island because she knows the local conditions and can fight for his survival. Amy agrees, giving Julie a final chance at redemption through sacrifice rather than possession.
